ja: רגל תזורה וחית השדה תדושה, הקשיח בניה ללא לה לריק יגיעה בלי פחד, כי השה אלוה חכמה ולא חלק לה בבינה. וקד מדח אלחכים מן כאן עלי כ'לאף הד'א פי חזמה וחסן אג'תהאדה פי ד'כ'אירה, ואמרנא באלאעתבאר בה ואלתאדב בפעלה ואן כאן אצ'עף אלחשראת, פי קולה לך אל נמלה עצל ראה דרכיה וחכם. וקד ד'כרת לך קלילא מן כת'יר, פלא תסתכת'רה ולא תברם פיה, פאן עלי חסב שרף אלצנאעה תכון אלאפאת אללאחקה להא, ומטלובנא פי הד'א אלבאב לא יכ'פי שרפה ופצ'לה עלי מן פהם. ג'עלנא אללה ואיאך מן אלמכ'לצין לה, ואלעאמלין לוג'הה תעאלי ברחמתה. כמל אלבאב אלכ'אמס פי שרח וג'וה וג'וב אכ'לאץ אלעמל לוג'ה אללה ואלתחפט' מן אלריא. ובכמאלה כמל אלג'זו אלאול מן כתאב אלהדאיה אלי פראיץ' אלקלוב בעון אללה ומנתה סבחאנה.
en_candidate:
The kingpin is *watchful awareness of God by the heart at the time of every act*. The body has its watchful awareness from the limbs whose movements people can see; the heart has its watchful awareness from God who searches the inward. To stand, at every act, in the consciousness that *God is watching*, and to perform the act with that consciousness as the operative interior — that is what makes the act, in its inwardness, a duty-of-the-heart performance and not merely a duty-of-the-limbs performance. The two duties may take place in a single act of, say, prayer; what distinguishes the prayer that is heart-and-limbs from the prayer that is limbs-only is the active *murāqaba* of God under whose gaze the prayer is taking place.

This concept will be developed in its proper gate (*Bāb al-murāqaba*, the Eighth Gate). What is required here is only the recognition that, without this watchful awareness, the work of *ikhlāṣ* in this gate cannot be completed — for the rest of the disciplines we have laid out are stratagems by the believer against his own caprice, and stratagems can be tricked. *Murāqaba*, by contrast, cannot be tricked: if one is genuinely standing under God's gaze, the question of *ikhlāṣ* is not a question one has to ask oneself, since the answer is settled by the gaze itself.

For this reason, the early ones said: "Know what is above you — a seeing eye, and a hearing ear, and all your deeds in a book are written" (m. Avot 2:1). The triple formula — *seeing eye, hearing ear, all deeds in a book* — is the rabbinic articulation of *murāqaba* applied to a Jewish-pious life: the believer who carries with him, at every moment, the consciousness that God sees, hears, and records, has built into his ordinary day the watchful awareness that this gate has been recommending. The Sufi teaching of *murāqaba* is not, in this respect, foreign to the rabbinic tradition; it is the same teaching, articulated in different vocabulary.
